claim: For the generalized Lorenz system \(\dot x=-s_1x+s_2y\), \(\dot y=Rx+dy-xz\), and \(\dot z=-qz+xy\), assume \(s_1>d>0\), \(q>0\), \(s_2\ne0\), and \(s_1d+s_2R>0\). Let \(z_*=R+s_1d/s_2\), the common height of the two nonzero equilibria. Every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies the exact defect law \[\int x^2(z-z_*)\,d\mu=\frac1{s_2}\int(-s_1x+s_2y)^2\,d\mu.\] Equality holds exactly for invariant probability measures supported on the three equilibria. Hence every non-equilibrium ergodic compact recurrent state has strict weighted-height bias: if \(s_2>0\), then \(\int x^2z\,d\mu/\int x^2\,d\mu>z_*\) and the state gives positive measure to \(z>z_*\); if \(s_2<0\), both inequalities reverse. In particular, every nonconstant periodic orbit must cross to the corresponding strict side of the nonzero-equilibrium height.
limitations: The law constrains compact invariant probability measures but does not prove existence of non-equilibrium recurrent dynamics for a specified parameter set. It gives a strict side-crossing condition, not a quantitative residence-time or excursion-amplitude bound. No claim is made for noncompactly supported measures without the required polynomial integrability.
scientific_integrity: The identity is obtained from an exact polynomial coboundary and the equality case is classified directly from the vector field. The source system and parameter regime were read from the full published paper. The symbolic checker verifies algebra only; no finite numerical trajectory is used as evidence for an infinite-time claim.
title: Weighted equilibrium-height defect for compact recurrence in a generalized Lorenz flow
